# Incident Report: 2024-08-15 Traffic Analysis Exercise

## 1. Victim Host
| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 | 10.8.15.133 |
| MAC address | 00:1c:bf:03:54:82 |
| Windows hostname | DESKTOP-H8ALZBV |
| AD domain | lafontainebleu.org (workgroup name seen in NBNS: LAFONTAINEBLEU) |
| Logged-in user | plucero (confirmed via Kerberos `CNameString`, both as `plucero` and `DESKTOP-H8ALZBV$` machine account) |

MAC bound to 10.8.15.133 confirmed via ARP; hostname confirmed independently via DHCP (option 12), NBNS, and DNS dynamic-update queries.

## 2. Malware Family
**Latrodectus** (loader/downloader malware, IcedID successor). Attribution is **behavioral, not signature-confirmed** — no IDS/Suricata alert files were present in the evidence directory, so this is based on TTP correlation:

- Fake-invoice phishing lure (FedEx-themed) delivering a ZIP containing a single obfuscated `.js` file — Latrodectus's standard initial-access pattern.
- The JS stage results in a `BITSAdmin`-driven download of a 64-bit PE32+ **DLL** from a bare-IP HTTP host (`User-Agent: Microsoft BITS/7.8`), matching Latrodectus's documented use of BITS jobs for payload retrieval/retry.
- Post-execution C2 beaconing uses a highly distinctive malformed User-Agent string, `Mozilla / 5.0 (compatible; MSIE 6.0; Windows NT 5.1; SV1; .NET CLR 1.0.3705)` (note the space around the slash), with encrypted binary payloads carried in a `Cookie:` header on GET requests and in the POST body — a known Latrodectus C2 protocol signature.

## 3. Indicators of Compromise (all observed directly in the capture)

### Delivery / phishing infrastructure
| Type | Indicator |
|---|---|
| Domain | `quote.checkfedexexp.com` |
| Domain | `business.checkfedexexp.com` |
| Resolved IPs (Cloudflare-fronted) | 104.21.55.70, 172.67.170.159 |
| Malicious URL | `http://quote.checkfedexexp.com/managements?16553a25e45250a41fd5&endeds=MIGpq&JStx=59bf050d37df88a9-ade43358-eaa1220b-0571422b-0f33e6aa150e86bafd0ed4&Ld=9d7502d88d752a27b1d00587309184b5a215` (t=74.7s) — served a ZIP archive |
| Transferred file (ZIP) | SHA256 `798563fcf7600f7ef1a35996291a9dfb5f9902733404dd499e2e736ea1dc6fc5` |
| Contained file | `Invoice-876597035-003-8331775-8334138.js` (inside the ZIP above) |
| TLS SNI contact (HTTPS) | `business.checkfedexexp.com` → 172.67.170.159 (t=100.3s) |

### Payload staging (BITS download)
| Type | Indicator |
|---|---|
| C2 / staging endpoint | 72.5.43.29:80 (bare-IP HTTP host, no domain) |
| URL | `http://72.5.43.29/data/0f60a3e7baecf2748b1c8183ed37d1e4` |
| Delivery mechanism | `User-Agent: Microsoft BITS/7.8` (HEAD then GET, repeated) |
| Transferred file | PE32+ DLL, x86-64, 159,232 bytes — SHA256 `b7aec5f73d2a6bbd8cd920edb4760e2edadc98c3a45bf4fa994d47ca9cbd02f6` |

### Command-and-control
| Type | Indicator |
|---|---|
| C2 endpoint | **72.5.43.29:80** |
| Beacon pattern | Hundreds of short-lived TCP sessions (ephemeral source ports 49810–50214) to the same IP:port over ~30 minutes, each with GET (encrypted data in `Cookie:` header) followed by POST (encrypted binary body) |
| C2 User-Agent | `Mozilla / 5.0 (compatible; MSIE 6.0; Windows NT 5.1; SV1; .NET CLR 1.0.3705)` |

## 4. Timeline Summary
1. t≈74.7s — 10.8.15.133 requests `quote.checkfedexexp.com/managements?...`, receives ZIP containing `Invoice-876597035-003-8331775-8334138.js`.
2. t≈100.3s — TLS session to `business.checkfedexexp.com` (172.67.170.159).
3. t≈134.8s — first BITS-driven HTTP transfer to 72.5.43.29, retrieving the malicious DLL (`/data/0f60a3e7baecf2748b1c8183ed37d1e4`).
4. t≈134.8s onward (duration ~1827s / ~30 min) — sustained GET/POST beaconing to 72.5.43.29:80 with encrypted payloads, consistent with active C2 tasking.

## 5. Benign Context (not indicators)
Traffic to Microsoft/Akamai/Adobe delivery and telemetry endpoints (`msedge.b.tlu.dl.delivery.mp.microsoft.com`, `oneocsp.microsoft.com`, `www.msftconnecttest.com`, `acroipm2.adobe.com`, LDAP/Kerberos/CLDAP/DCE-RPC to 10.8.15.4) is normal Windows/AD/Office background activity and is not part of the infection chain.
